clue.text: Publicly retract previous opinion of the city in bombastic speech

indicators.note: the bombastic speech is opened up so that the city sits within it

parts.note: a rant is a loud, bombastic speech
EC is the postcode for the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: A politician publicly takes back a stance once aired in a grandiose speech about the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The city' is the City of London, whose postal district is EC; 'in' places it inside RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw formally a belief or statement once held.

clue.text: Spanish wine jar I smashed when empty

indicators.note: a smashed jar is broken into pieces, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: something empty holds nothing, and nothing is the letter O

explanation.surface: A jar of Spanish wine gets broken once it has been drunk dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' rearranges JAR and I together with O, the zero that 'empty' stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the region of that name in northern Spain.

clue.text: Insects found under tea cup

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that is under comes below, so the insects follow the tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Bugs are discovered beneath a teacup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' in a down clue puts LICE below CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a large drinking cup or goblet, often used in church.

clue.text: Mean article to reveal narrow escape

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy or mean with money
an article is an object, a thing

explanation.surface: A petty piece of writing exposes a close shave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb or an average; it is stingy, NEAR. 'Article' suggests a grammar word, but here it is an object, THING.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a situation where disaster was only just avoided.

clue.text: Compassionate chap put in the shade

indicators.note: the chap is placed into the shade, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted fellow is moved out of the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in the shade' reads as outshone, but 'put in' places MAN inside HUE, a shade of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Humane means showing kindness and mercy towards others.

clue.text: The custom which is as old as America itself

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States of America
how old a thing is is its age

explanation.surface: A tradition that has existed as long as the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The age of America, US AGE, reads as one word meaning custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is habitual practice, the customary way something is done.

clue.text: Maintains a rising pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for pressure is read from bottom to top

parts.note: stress is pressure or strain

explanation.surface: Someone insists that pressure is increasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns STRESS into SSERTS, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a view is to declare it firmly, to insist on it.

clue.text: Package turned up, given address with added detail

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word for package is read upwards

parts.note: a bale is a large bound package of goods
to orate is to address an audience formally

explanation.surface: A parcel arrives and is given a delivery address with some extra particulars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reverses BALE to ELAB; 'address' is a verb, to make a speech, ORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate is intricate, worked out with many particulars.

clue.text: Obtained a route and escaped

parts.note: got is a synonym of obtained
a way is a route

explanation.surface: Someone found a path and fled.
explanation.definitionFit: To have got away is to have fled, slipped free.

clue.text: He has to stay in to take delivery

definitions.text: He has to stay in to take delivery

parts.words: He has to stay in to take delivery
parts.note: reads as someone waiting at home for a parcel; in cricket the man who stays in (is not out) faces the bowler's delivery

explanation.surface: A man waits at home for a package.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a 'delivery' is a ball bowled, and a player who is 'in' is still batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket batter must avoid being out and faces each ball the bowler sends down.

clue.text: Feathered game

parts.note: reads as game birds such as pheasant; it is a sport played with a feathered shuttlecock

explanation.surface: Game birds with plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: This racket sport is played with a shuttlecock made of feathers.

clue.text: Justice obtained by a soldier in various matters

indicators.note: the soldier with the a is placed within the rearranged matters
various suggests diverse forms, so the letters of matters are rearranged

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: Legal redress secured by a serviceman across several cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges MATTERS into M...STRATE; 'in' puts A and GI between M and STRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A justice of the peace is a lay magistrate who hears minor cases.

clue.text: When corruption is about I show no respect for authority

indicators.note: the word for corruption goes round the I, surrounding it

parts.note: rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: When there is graft around, I defy the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts ROT around I.
explanation.definitionFit: To riot is to rise up violently against public order and those in charge.

clue.text: Nigerians hold the French back with daggers drawn

indicators.note: back means the whole combination is then read in reverse
the Nigerians hold the French word, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Ibo (Igbo) are a people of Nigeria
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Nigerians keep the French at bay, with hostility at its height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' puts LE inside IBO, giving ILEBO; 'back' reverses that. 'At daggers drawn' means hostile, but here the daggers are printed marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger-shaped printers' symbols, used to mark footnotes or doubtful passages.

clue.text: Smile upon frolic that's spontaneous

indicators.note: to frolic is to romp about, so the letters caper into a new order

explanation.surface: A grin breaks into play on a sudden whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frolic' rearranges SMILE and UPON together.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on a whim means acting without forethought, which is what spontaneous describes.

clue.text: The most important guy on board

definitions.meaning: a chief support, the thing everything depends on
on a sailing ship, the rope bracing the mainmast, a stay or guy

explanation.surface: The key man on the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'guy' is a supporting rope, and 'on board' means on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief prop or support, and literally the rigging rope that steadies a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Fashionable with-it person encountered on the cricket field

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a swinger is a lively, trendy person

explanation.surface: A trendy, up-to-date type met on the cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an inswinger is a ball that curves in the air towards the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: This type of ball bowled in cricket is a common sight at any match.

clue.text: Superior neighbour in the US

parts.note: reads as a better-off person next door; it is one of the Great Lakes that borders Lake Superior

explanation.surface: A better-class person living next door in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' is Lake Superior, one of the Great Lakes, and its neighbour is another lake and the state of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Michigan lies beside Lake Superior, and the state of Michigan borders it.

clue.text: Pelt American all round ring? That's horrid

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's skin, a hide
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: An American skin worn all round a ring is an ugly sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a verb, to throw, but it is a noun, HIDE. 'All round' puts US around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideous means extremely ugly or dreadful, much like horrid.

clue.text: Notes removed by a dentist

definitions.meaning: a series of musical notes rising or falling in order
the hard deposit scraped from teeth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like messages; here it is music.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical run of notes in order, and the tartar a hygienist scrapes off teeth.

clue.text: Is a back number, being stupid

indicators.note: back means the words is and a are read in reverse order

parts.note: nine is a number

explanation.surface: Being an old edition of a magazine is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A back number' suggests an old issue, but 'back' reverses IS A into ASI, then NINE is the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means foolish, like a donkey.

clue.text: Murphy turns up in South Dakota

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota

indicators.note: turns means the word up is read backwards

explanation.surface: A man named Murphy appears in South Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murphy' is slang for a potato, from the Irish surname. 'Turns' reverses UP to PU, which goes 'in' SD.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud and murphy are both informal names for a potato.

clue.text: Primitive sailor of marked individuality

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
an original person is distinctive and unique

explanation.surface: A rough, uncivilised seaman with a strong character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor' gives AB, able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboriginal means existing from the earliest times, primeval.

clue.text: Around or around

explanation.walkthrough: The same word twice, in two senses: approximately and nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: It means roughly (approximately so many) and also near or here and there.

clue.text: One advantage of adjust able seats

indicators.note: adjustable things can be rearranged, so the letters of seats are reordered

explanation.surface: A benefit of seats you can adjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adjust able' (printed as two words) is the anagram signal on SEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or thing, a benefit.

clue.text: Where is this sold? Oh, in the local, perhaps

definitions.text: Where is this sold? Oh, in the local, perhaps

indicators.note: the exclamation is placed inside the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests one possible arrangement, so the letters of local are shuffled

explanation.surface: A question about where something is sold, answered by the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges LOCAL to ALCOL; 'in' places OH inside. The 'local' is British for one's neighbourhood pub, where drink is sold.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer, wine and spirits are sold in a pub.

clue.text: Anti-cooking, anti-gas

indicators.note: cooking suggests something being cooked up, so the letters are mixed afresh

explanation.surface: A slogan opposing cooking and gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' rearranges ANTI and GAS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Against means opposed to, like the prefix for opposition.

clue.text: Not the genuine article from bankers at Zurich

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A fake supplied by Swiss bankers.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'bankERS AT Zurich'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz means a substitute, an imitation of the real thing.

clue.text: Stop a criminal proceeding

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop a criminal' reads as one phrase, but the split is after 'Stop'.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt something, and the act of police taking someone into custody.
